extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing or responding to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form‑paragraphs for making and supporting rejections under the pre‑AIA versions of 35 U.S.C. 102 (paragraphs (a)–(g)), including date‑determinations, benefit/priority claims, procedural ordering of form paragraphs, and how to handle copending applications, public use/on‑sale, abandonment, foreign patenting, and inventorship issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date for U.S. patent from national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly from a national stage of an international application, the reference’s pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date is the date that the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled. The language of WIPO publication (PCT) is not relevant in this situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: the international publication of the international application (PCT) by WIPO may have an earlier prior art date under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or pre‑AIA 102(b). Use the date the 371(c) requirements were met to determine the pre‑AIPA 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date for patent issued from continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly from a continuing application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) to such an international application (which had not entered the national stage prior to the continuing application’s filing date), the prior art reference’s pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date is the actual U.S. filing date of the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: the international publication of the international application (PCT) by WIPO may have an earlier prior art date under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or pre‑AIA 102(b). Apply proper statutes to determine which prior art date controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of benefit/priority claims and written‑description support
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider benefit claims to earlier‑filed U.S. provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), and to earlier‑filed U.S. nonprovisional applications and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied upon earlier‑filed application’s disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A benefit claim to a U.S. patent of an earlier‑filed international application may only result in an effective U.S. filing date as of the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4) were fulfilled. Do NOT consider benefit claims to U.S. applications which are filed before an international application. Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)‑(d), 365(a) or (b), or 386(a) or (b). In addition, a reference is entitled to the benefit of the filing date of a provisional application only if at least one of the claims in the reference is supported by the written description of the provisional application in compliance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph or 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (see Dynamic Drinkware; Amgen v. Sanofi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural ordering: required preceding form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs for rejections must be preceded by specific other form paragraphs (e.g., many 7.1x.fti paragraphs must be preceded by 7.07.fti and may require 7.08.fti–7.12.fti or 7.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using a form paragraph for a rejection, ensure the required preceding form paragraph(s) are included (examples shown throughout: 7.13.fti, 7.14.fti, 7.15.fti and its variants refer to required precedents such as 7.07.fti, 7.08.fti–7.12.fti, 7.06, or 7.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f): Applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) — the applicant did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti, and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08.fti to 7.12.fti. Provide supporting evidence and explanation (see MPEP §2137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g): Priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) where, during interference practice, another inventor establishes that the invention was made by such other inventor before the applicant’s invention, and not abandoned, suppressed or concealed, or that the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed or concealed it. Consider conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining priority consider dates of conception and reduction to practice and the reasonable diligence of one who was first to conceive and last to reduce to practice. This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08.fti to 7.13.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of a pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b)/(g) rejection (¶7.15.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template rejection: 'Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].' Bracket fields specify which paragraph, whether 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation, and identify the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by required form paragraph(s) (7.07.fti and appropriate others) or by form paragraph 7.103. If pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) is also applied, follow with one of 7.15.01/02/03.fti. For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 claiming benefit to an application filed before that date, precede by form paragraph 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection over copending application (¶7.15.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as anticipated by a copending application which has a common assignee, common applicant, or at least one common (joint) inventor; the copending application would constitute prior art if published or patented, so the provisional rejection is based on a presumption of future publication/patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome either by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of this application (not 'by another'), or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131(a). This rejection may NOT be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Examiner Notes: use only where copending app discloses claimed invention and has common assignee/applicant or at least one common inventor; apply AIPA/Technical Amendments rules to determine the reference’s 102(e) date; if claims would have been obvious over disclosures in the copending app use the obviousness form paragraphs; handle identical subject matter and nonstatutory double patenting per the cited form paragraphs (8.30–8.39, 8.27.fti, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection over issued patent/publication with common assignee/applicant/inventor (¶7.15.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by an applied reference that has a common assignee, common applicant, or a common (joint) inventor with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be overcome by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventive entity of this application (not 'by another'), or by showing under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Apply amendments to pre‑AIA 102(e) (AIPA, Technical Amendments) to determine dates; consider benefit claims and provisional support requirements. If the reference is a PCT/unpublished international app with certain characteristics, do not apply 102(e) (see notes). Handle identical subject matter and nonstatutory double patenting per form paragraphs 8.30–8.39 and 8.27.fti. Patent application publications may be used only if preceded by form paragraph 7.12.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection over earlier‑filed patent/application with no common assignee/inventor (¶7.15.03.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being [clearly anticipated/anticipated] by an earlier patent or patent application publication that is not required to have a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the AIPA/Technical Amendments rules (7.12.fti) where applicable to determine the reference’s 102(e) date; apply pre‑AIPA rules (7.12.01.fti) for international applications filed prior to Nov. 29, 2000. Consider benefit claims to earlier filings only if the subject matter is supported in the earlier disclosures. If the reference is a PCT publication that did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English, do not use this form paragraph; instead apply under pre‑AIA 102(a) or (b). Provide explanation of anticipation (insert 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation) and identify the prior art relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for public use or on sale (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.09.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in bracket 2. See MPEP sections on public use/on‑sale for detailed factors (e.g., experimental use, intent, completeness of invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for abandonment of the invention (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraph 7.07.fti and 7.10.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2, insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment of the invention. See MPEP §2134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for foreign patenting (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants' foreign patent filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.11.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. In bracket 3, insert an explanation including appropriate dates and how they make the foreign patent available under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d). Refer to MPEP §2135 for applicable prior art rules under 102(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for applicant not the inventor (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f)) (¶7.19.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded either by paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.13.fti or by paragraph 7.103. In bracket 2, insert an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP §2137 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling identical subject matter and nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 101, two patents are not permitted to issue on identical subject matter. Claims directed to the same invention claimed in the reference should be provisionally rejected and applicants required to amend or cancel claims; claims not patentably distinct should be rejected on nonstatutory double patenting grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32 for provisional rejection of identical subject matter; require amendment or cancellation of claims using form paragraph 8.27.fti. For nonstatutory double patenting use form paragraph 8.33 and at least one of form paragraphs 8.34–8.39. If evidence shows prior art under 102(f) or (g), make corresponding rejections using form paragraphs 7.13.fti and/or 7.14.fti. See MPEP §804 and related sections for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions and means to overcome provisional rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejections based on copending applications rely on a presumption of future publication/patenting or on the applied reference having a prior art date; such provisional rejections can be rebutted by specific showings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible rebuttals include: showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention in the other copending application was derived from the inventive entity of the instant application (not 'by another'), or an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Note that a terminal disclaimer cannot overcome certain provisional rejections (In re Bartfeld). If obviousness is at issue rather than anticipation, use the obviousness form paragraphs (e.g., 7.21.01.fti).
